North Korea Fires Ballistic Missile, Cites Japan's 'Transformation'

North Korea fired a ballistic missile into the East Sea on Wednesday, according to South Korea's military. State media quoted Kim Yo Jong, sister of leader Kim Jong Un, stating that Pyongyang would "set up additional military options" due to Japan's "transformation." The missile was described as short-range by Seoul. The specific nature of Japan's "transformation" was not detailed in the coverage.
